items.title: Section: The Marks of Entry Open — Two Signs a Lineage-Bearer Has Truly Begun

items.zh: 云何名為已趣入者所有諸相？謂安住種姓補特伽羅纔已趣入，設轉餘生，於自大師及善說法毘奈耶中，雖復妄念。若遇世間現有惡說法毘奈耶，及有善說法毘奈耶，雖久聽聞以無量門讚美惡說法毘奈耶有勝功德，而不信解愛樂修行，亦不於彼而求出家。設暫出家，纔得趣入，尋復速疾棄捨退還。為性於彼不樂安住。如蜜生蟲置之釅酢；或如愛樂受妙欲者，置淤泥中。彼由宿世妙善因力所任持故。若暫聽聞讚美善說法毘奈耶少分功德，或全未聞。雖暫少聞，或全未聞，而能速疾信解趣入，愛樂修行，或求出家。既出家已，畢竟趣入，終無退轉。為性於此愛樂安住。如蜜生蟲置之上蜜；或如愛樂受妙欲者，置勝欲中。彼由宿世妙善因力所任持故。是名第一已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。復有所餘已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。謂雖未得能往一切惡趣、無暇煩惱離繫，而能不生惡趣、無暇。世尊依此已得趣入補特伽羅，密意說言：若有世間上品正見，雖歷千生不墮惡趣。
items.en: What are the marks possessed by one who has entered? It is that a person abiding in lineage, having just entered, even if reborn in a further life … should that person encounter, in the world, both an existing tradition of wrongly-taught doctrine and discipline, and one rightly taught — even after long hearing wrongly-taught doctrine and discipline praised from countless angles as possessing excellent qualities — does not believe in it, does not delight in practising it, and does not seek to go forth within it. …Such a person is, by nature, unable to delight in dwelling there — like a maggot born in honey, placed into strong vinegar; or like one who delights in enjoying fine sensory pleasures, placed into a muddy swamp. …Should that person hear, even briefly, the rightly-taught doctrine and discipline praised for even a small portion of its virtue — or hear nothing of it at all — that person is nonetheless able swiftly to believe, to enter, to delight in practising it, or to seek to go forth within it. …Such a person is, by nature, able to delight in dwelling there — like a maggot born in honey, placed into the finest honey; or like one who delights in enjoying fine sensory pleasures, placed amid excellent pleasures. This is because such a person is sustained by the power of excellent causes planted in past lives. This is called the first mark possessed by a person who has entered. …Though not yet having attained freedom from the bonds of affliction that lead to every unfortunate rebirth and every state without leisure, such a person is nonetheless able to avoid being reborn into unfortunate rebirths or states without leisure. Resting on this, the Bhagavat, speaking with hidden intent, said of such a person who has entered: "One who possesses a superior grade of mundane correct view will not fall into an unfortunate rebirth even after passing through a thousand lifetimes."

items.zh: 彼若已入上品善根，漸向成熟，爾時便能不生無暇及餘惡趣。是名第二已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。復有所餘已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。

items.title: Marks Three Through Seven: A Devotion That Moves the Body, and a Character Reshaped From Within

items.zh: 謂暫聞佛或法或僧勝功德已，便得隨念清淨信心，引發廣大出離善法。數數緣念，融練淨心，身遂毛竪、悲泣雨淚。是名第三已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。復有所餘已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。謂性成就猛利慚愧，於所現行諸有罪處，深生羞恥。是名第四已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。復有所餘已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。謂於受持、讀誦、請問、思惟、觀行、求善法中，有深欲樂、猛利欲樂。是名第五已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。復有所餘已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。謂於一切無罪事業，修集一切善品加行正方便中，能善修集，堅固發起、長時發起、決定發起。是名第六已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。復有所餘已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。謂彼為性塵垢微薄，煩惱羸劣。雖起諸纏，而不長時相續久住。無諂無誑，能制憍慢我我所執。好取功德，憎背過失。是名第七已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。
items.en: It is that, upon merely hearing of the Buddha's, the Dharma's, or the Saṅgha's excellent qualities, one attains a pure faith arising from recollection, drawing forth vast, world-transcending wholesome states. Recollecting again and again, refining and purifying the mind, the body's hairs stand on end, and one weeps tears like rain. This is the third mark. It is that one's nature has fully developed keen shame and conscience, feeling deep humiliation at whatever wrongdoing one has actually done. This is the fourth mark. …It is that, in upholding, reciting, questioning, reflecting, contemplating, and seeking wholesome states, one has a deep and keen aspiration. This is the fifth mark. …It is that, in every blameless activity, in cultivating the correct means of applying oneself to every wholesome state, one is able to cultivate it well — arousing it firmly, arousing it over a long time, arousing it decisively. This is the sixth mark. …It is that such a person is, by nature, one whose defiling dust is slight and whose afflictions are feeble; though entanglements do arise, they do not persist for long. Free of flattery, free of deceit, able to control pride and attachment to self and what is one's own, delighting in acquiring virtue, disdaining and turning away from fault. This is the seventh mark.

items.zh: 復有所餘已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。

items.title: Section: The Eighth Mark Closes the List — Three Grades, and Only a Buddha Can See Them All

items.zh: 謂能善巧藏護其心，於諸廣大所應證處不自輕蔑，不自安處無力能中，其所信解增多猛盛。是名第八已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。如是等類已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相，當知無量，我於是中已說少分。如是諸相，若有安住下品善根而趣入者，當知下品，名有間隙，未能無間，未善清淨。若有安住中品善根而趣入者，當知中品。若有安住上品善根而趣入者，當知上品，無有間隙，已能無間，已善清淨。如是名為已得趣入補特伽羅已趣入相。成就如是趣入相者，當知墮在已趣入數。應知如是安住種姓、已得趣入補特伽羅所有眾多吉祥士相，唯佛世尊及到第一究竟弟子，以善清淨勝妙智見，現見現證。
items.en: It is that one is skilfully able to guard and protect one's own mind — regarding all the vast attainments yet to be realised, neither disparaging oneself, nor placing oneself among those without the capacity, one's own confidence and understanding growing ever more abundant and vigorous. This is the eighth mark possessed by a person who has entered. …Regarding these marks: if one abides in a lower grade of wholesome roots and enters, this should be understood as the lower grade — marked by gaps, not yet uninterrupted, not yet well purified. If one abides in a middle grade of wholesome roots and enters, this should be understood as the middle grade. If one abides in a higher grade of wholesome roots and enters, this should be understood as the higher grade — free of gaps, already uninterrupted, already well purified. These are called the marks possessed by a person who has entered. …It should be understood that these many auspicious marks, belonging to a person abiding in lineage who has entered, are directly seen and directly confirmed only by the buddha-bhagavats and by disciples who have reached the very peak of realisation, through their well-purified, most excellent wisdom and vision.

items.zh: 隨其種姓，隨所趣入，如應救濟。

items.title: Fascicle Complete: The Ground of Entry Closes at the Fascicle's True End

items.zh: 云何名為已得趣入補特伽羅？謂或有已得趣入補特伽羅，唯已趣入，未將成熟，未已成熟，未得出離。或有亦已趣入，亦將成熟，未已成熟，未得出離。或有亦已趣入，亦已成熟，未得出離、隨欲而行。如是差別，應知如前已辨其相。復有所餘，如種姓地說軟根等補特伽羅所有差別，今於此中，如其所應，亦當了知所有差別。如是所說若趣入自性、若趣入安立、若已趣入者所有諸相、若已趣入補特伽羅，一切總說名趣入地。
items.en: What is called a person who has entered? There is a person who has only entered, not yet about to ripen, not yet already ripened, not yet freed. There is one who has both entered and is about to ripen, not yet already ripened, not yet freed. There is one who has both entered and is already ripened, not yet freed, and who cannot yet act freely as one wishes. …There are, further, other differences, just as explained in the Ground of Spiritual Lineage for persons of weak faculties and the rest — these should likewise be understood here, exactly as applicable. Thus, whether it is the intrinsic nature of entry, or the establishment of entry, or the marks possessed by one who has entered, or the persons who have entered — all of this together is called the Ground of Entry.

blocks.text: How can one tell that someone has truly entered the path? The treatise gives eight signs. The fascicle and the Stage of Entry end today.

Like "a maggot born in honey, placed into strong vinegar", such a person cannot delight in what is contrary to the Dharma; "placed into the finest honey", they delight in it. Master Cháng Bǎi links this to the stages of "heat" and "summit" in the *Kośa*: heat surely reaches nirvāṇa; the summit never severs wholesome roots.

"Upon merely hearing of the excellent qualities of the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Saṅgha, one attains pure faith arising from recollection": hair stands on end, tears fall. The person's character changes: the "dust" (manifest affliction) and "grime" (seeds) are thin (Master Cháng Bǎi). Such a one is free of flattery and deceit, takes instruction well, and finds joy in practice.

"One is able to guard one's own mind: regarding the attainments yet to be realised, neither disparaging oneself nor exalting oneself." Each mark has three grades: the lower "marked by gaps, not yet uninterrupted", the higher "free of gaps, already well purified". Only a Buddha can see all of them; we cannot. Venerable Miào Jìng suggests that the "foremost disciple" capable of such vision would be one like Maitreya.

Lineage and entry: who can practise, under what conditions, and how to recognise a real beginning. The next fascicle starts the third part, the **Stage of Departure** (出離地), and the long account of how one actually trains.

quiz.q: What simile does the treatise use for the first mark of one who has entered?
options: like a honey-born grub placed in strong vinegar, unhappy; placed in fine honey, content — averse to wrong teaching, delighting in right teaching
quiz.why: "Like a maggot born in honey, placed into strong vinegar" — unable to delight in dwelling there; "placed into the finest honey" — able to delight. Master Cháng Bǎi: non-Buddhist teachings are like strong vinegar, the Buddha's like honey.

quiz.q: The second mark says one who has entered, though not yet free of the bonds, is not reborn in bad destinies. Which treatise does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: the Kośa: heat surely reaches nirvāṇa, summit never cuts off good, patience never falls to bad destinies, the highest worldly stage enters the path
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the *Kośa* says: heat surely reaches nirvāṇa, the summit never severs good, patience does not fall to bad destinies, and the highest worldly stage enters the path. Venerable Miào Jìng: such a person has not severed these afflictions — that requires stream-entry — yet is not born in bad destinies.

quiz.q: What is the third mark of one who has entered?
options: merely hearing of the Three Jewels' qualities, pure faith arises; recollecting again and again, the hairs stand on end and tears fall like rain
quiz.why: "Upon merely hearing of the Buddha's, the Dharma's, or the Saṅgha's excellent qualities, one attains a pure faith arising from recollection… Recollecting again and again, refining and purifying the mind, the body's hairs stand on end, and one weeps tears like rain."

quiz.q: For the seventh mark, "defiling dust is slight," how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 塵 and 垢?
options: dust is manifest affliction, grime its seeds — both slight in such a person
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: such a person's character is that the dust (manifest activity) and grime (seeds) of affliction are slight and few. Free of flattery and deceit means a simple, upright nature.

quiz.q: According to the eighth mark, how does one who has entered regard "the vast attainments yet to be realised"?
options: guards the mind skilfully, neither disparaging oneself nor placing oneself among the incapable, confidence growing ever stronger
quiz.why: "One is skilfully able to guard and protect one's own mind — regarding all the vast attainments yet to be realised, neither disparaging oneself, nor placing oneself among those without the capacity, one's confidence growing ever more abundant." Master Cháng Bǎi: one does not belittle oneself as incapable.

quiz.q: How does the treatise distinguish the marks of those who enter with lower versus higher roots?
options: lower: with gaps, not yet uninterrupted, not well purified; higher: without gaps, uninterrupted, well purified
quiz.why: The lower grade is "marked by gaps, not yet uninterrupted, not yet well purified"; the higher "free of gaps, already uninterrupted, already well purified." Master Cháng Bǎi: the lower grade's wholesome roots have breaks and gaps — sometimes present, sometimes not.

quiz.q: Those who can directly see these auspicious marks are the buddhas and "disciples who have reached the foremost ultimate." The note says a peak arhat. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: it should be Maitreya, a bodhisattva of near-perfect awakening
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this foremost, most excellent ultimate disciple of the Buddha should be Maitreya — a bodhisattva of near-perfect awakening, one may say. This differs from the note's arhat.
